descs.t: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa says every datacenter already permitted in Texas will be allowed to finish construction, one of her first signals since Democrats flipped the state in the midterms. Polling accounts say no part of Texas failed to shift blue. This video walks through the result, her promise and what changes next for the state.

Democrats now hold power in Texas, and governor-elect Gina Hinojosa's first message went to datacenter builders: permitted projects will finish. On the right, accounts point to the new State Board of Education and the mandatory Bible inclusion in schools, while others push fraud claims. This video sorts what the new majority can do from what is only being claimed.

Texas flipped blue, and the fight over what it means started at once. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa says permitted datacenters will be built, one account says a blue State Board of Education can cancel the mandatory Bible inclusion in schools, and others claim fraud. This video walks through each claim and what it means for religion in public schools and the freedom to build.

intro.plain: Texas flipped blue on Tuesday, and the governor-elect, Gina Hinojosa, has already sent her first signal: every datacenter already permitted in the state gets to finish construction. Democrats shifted the whole map, some on the right are claiming fraud, and Republicans are already floating names for 2030. So, live chat, tell me: did you see this coming in Texas?
intro.mid: Texas is blue, and one of the first things governor-elect Gina Hinojosa said was that permitted datacenters will finish. That tells you something about how she wants to govern. The bigger fight may be in schools, where a blue State Board of Education could undo the mandatory Bible inclusion. Chat, what should a new Texas majority change first, and what should it leave alone?
intro.bold: Texas. Blue. Let that sink in. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa says the datacenters keep building, accounts on the right are already shouting fraud, and the Bible mandate in public schools may be on the way out. Religion in a classroom should never be the state's call. Chat, was this a protest vote about the war and gas prices, or a real shift?

hook.plain: Texas flipped blue, and its new governor-elect's first promise was not about schools or the border. It was about datacenters. Here is what she said and what the new majority can change.
